On Mon, May 16, 2027 at 9:37 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether you pasted the Meet link into the invite description or if the Google-generated Meet link was attached?

Short answer: if the organizer's calendar is on a different Google Workspace domain, you can't transfer organizer rights and Google may strip or replace Meet tokens when events are forwarded between domains. We've seen two common patterns and the remediation steps below:

- If the Meet link was created by LedgerWave's GSuite at invite creation time: ask them to EDIT the original event and re-save (this should re-populate the active Meet link) — they must do the edit from the org that created the event.
- If their calendar system exported an .ics with a statically embedded link that expired: they should re-export the invite or paste a stable (non-expiring) Zoom link.

Workaround I created: I generated a Zoom meeting for Wed 5/18 11am PT (link below) and put a short fallback invite that Nikhil can forward from redwood.ai. That avoids organizer-transfer issues. Let me know if Alyssa's firm requires SSO-enabled Zoom — if so we can send a pro-auth link.

Zoom fallback: https://zoom.us/j/999999999
Attachment: alt-zoom-link.txt (contains join info and dial-in)

Ethan — can you confirm there's no calendar-level block that will stop our forwarding the new invite to Alyssa's list?
